title: (console-era remnant, save format): Nebula's save is the console's GameData.bin layout in host order: attribute names as 16-bit hashes with u16 offsets (BinaryDataContentAccessor.cpp:13-20, :55-64), galaxy records keyed by a 16-bit hash (GameDataGalaxyStorage.cpp:184), chunk counts in a byte (BinaryDataChunkHolder.cpp:46-49), spin-driver ids masked to 6 bits (SpinDriverPathStorage.cpp:55), event values as u16 (GameEventValueChecker.cpp:48-53).
note: Found by the inventory's pass two (the Game/Screen whole read, 11-18, every line cited read at 6577392b5). The readall harness found the same lines (BinaryDataChunkHolder, BinaryDataContentAccessor, GameDataGalaxyStorage, GameEventValueChecker, SpinDriverPathStorage). Not in CONSOLE-FREE.md (only the 60.75 MHz times and the Vector list). Modern form: the save as named, sized records with a version; an old file read once by the importer; 5.H.3: mods' galaxies, values and drivers need no hash space, offset width or id mask. 11-18 (the harness's System report, checked at 241395b49): event flags under a 15-bit name hash, the top bit their state (GameEventFlagTable.cpp:586, GameEventFlagStorage.cpp:33-34; P-232's collision); the galaxy chunk written with no bound against its room (GameDataAllGalaxyStorage::serialize ignores dataSize, GameDataGalaxyStorage.cpp:367-388). 11-18 (the harness's platform/android report, checked at 241395b49): the game still reads a console GameData.bin at load from the NAND layout's folder (save_files.h:37-39, "/title/00010000/<the code in hex>/data"; host_main.cpp:3521, :6187; the read names at SaveDataHandler.cpp:21-23), the Wii's big-endian or the Switch release's little-endian version 2 told apart by SaveFileFormat.hpp:35-39; Android's save import writes a console file there as it is (SaveTransfer.kt:103, :177-194) and keeps title and shared2 as save top folders (:278-279). Modern form: the import turns a console file once into Nebula.sav in the release's folder, the NAND layout known only to the importer, on every platform (save_transfer.cpp too).

title: (wrong save data, hashes taken for names): GameEventValueChecker::deserialize reads size / 2 entries of four bytes (GameEventValueChecker.cpp:75-91), twice what the chunk holds; SaveReader gives zeros past the end (SaveBytes.hpp:67-73), hash 0 is not found, so every load marks the chunk failed, and the holder takes status 1 as success as it does 0 (BinaryDataChunkHolder.cpp:56-66), so no chunk's failure of that kind is ever seen. An event flag is saved under a 15-bit hash of its name (GameEventFlagTable.cpp:586; the top bit holds its state, GameEventFlagStorage.cpp:33-34), while a flag added at run time is checked free only by its 32-bit name hash (nameIsFree, GameEventFlagTable.cpp:336-349): two flags with one save hash are saved twice under it and a load sets the first (getIndexFromHashCode, :589-591). ResourceHolderManager::find takes the 32-bit lower-case hash for the name, with no compare (ResourceHolderManager.cpp:144-154): two archives with one hash are one. Also: the growth of the mapped-asset and arena lists does not check realloc (GameAssets.cpp:110-113, NebulaArena.cpp:115-118).
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/System report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Fix: entries counted by their size (size / 4); a chunk's failure reported as one; flags saved by name or by an id checked unique across the table and every mod's flags at load (P-205's save form); names compared after a hash match; allocation failures checked.

title: (frame budget at 60 Hz, cutscene skip; waits on the game thread): the cutscene skip runs its unseen steps for up to 9 ms of wall time and 40 steps a frame (NebulaCutsceneSkip.cpp:46-47, tryExtraStep :384-399), a fixed share that fits a 16.7 ms frame and is more than a whole frame above about 110 Hz. A save or load request waits on the game thread for the one before it (SaveDataHandler.cpp:120-122, from :129 and :534).
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/System report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Modern form: the skip's budget a share of the measured frame interval (the frame pacer's); a request queued behind the running one, the step never waiting. Replay identical (the skip's steps are the same, only how many a frame).

title: (a stuck save holds the game with no bound): the game's wait for its last save request sleeps until the worker ends it (svc_save_wait, host_main.cpp:3490-3495; StatusBoard::wait, save_files.cpp:179-186, a condition wait with no time limit), on the game thread; every way out waits a second and then for as long as the save takes (host_main.cpp:4739-4748), while the comment over the exits says the wait is bounded so that a dead drive does not hold the game (:4402). A write stuck on a vanished network folder or a removed card freezes the step, or the exit, for good.
note: Found by the readall harness's native/host report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Modern form: a bounded wait in both places; past it the player is told a save is being written and chooses to wait or quit, and the game's own save flow turns a stuck write into its save-failed message; the comments made to agree. Replay identical.
